title: Silverpine Health - SOC 2 / ISO 27001 Posture Review
next_steps: Send SOC 2 Type II report and ISO 27001 certificate via secure link
Share controls mapping spreadsheet aligning Redwood controls to Silverpine requirements
Schedule infra architecture deep-dive with Silverpine platform team (Ravi + Daniel)
Provide Trust Center access URL and temporary read-only account
Confirm CMK (customer-managed key) support and region-specific KMS options
action_items: Maya Chen — Send security package (SOC2 Type II, ISO27001) — due 2025-12-10
Ravi Patel — Prepare controls mapping spreadsheet and notes for architecture call — due 2025-12-12
Daniel Ortiz (Silverpine) — Share current network CIDRs, SIEM endpoint, and compliance contact — due 2025-12-11
summary: Redwood (AE + SE) walked Silverpine through SOC 2 and ISO 27001 posture, discussed trust center access, controls mapping, RBAC/SSO integration, audit log delivery and retention, and encryption/KMS options including customer-managed keys and data residency. Action items: send certs, share mapping, schedule infra deep-dive.
topics: SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 certificates
Data residency and private deployment options
transcript:
00:00 Maya Chen: Hey everyone thanks for carving out time, this is Maya from Redwood. We have Ravi with me. we're here to run through our SOC two and ISO posture and get a sense for any gaps on Silverpine's side.
00:10 Laura Kim: Hey Maya, thanks. I'm Laura, Head of Security. We also have Daniel, Priya and Ethan on the line. High level: we need to validate scope for a pilot and ensure our data residency plus KMS needs are covered.
00:22 Maya Chen: Great, can you remind us of the scope? which environments and what data classification?
00:27 Daniel Ortiz: Sure - for pilot it's metadata and de-identified patient notes; PII is redacted but we still need SOC2 coverage, ISO mapping, and audit logging forwarded to our Splunk instance.
00:40 Ravi Patel: Okay good, quick note - Redwood supports streaming audit logs and we can push via Kinesis, S3 delivery or direct syslog to a customer SIEM, there's a small config piece. We'll cover retention and fields.
00:55 Priya Sharma: On keys - do you support customer-managed keys? We can't have Redwood hold root encryption keys for production.
01:03 Maya Chen: Short answer yes, we support CMK via AWS KMS today for Hosted in supported regions, and Dedicated/Private also supports BYOK/HSM integrations. There are some caveats around key rotation and cross-region replication; we'll detail in the controls mapping doc.
01:20 Laura Kim: Do you have a SOC 2 Type II? and is ISO 27001 cert in scope? we want the actual attestation and evidence or access to a trust center.
01:29 Maya Chen: We have SOC 2 Type II for Redwood (report available under NDA) and ISO 27001 certificate; we can provide both and give Trust Center access - temporary read-only account for security teams to view artifacts. We'll send links.
01:41 Ethan Cho: How granular is RBAC? We need separation between app engineers and data scientists and admin-level roles.
01:48 Ravi Patel: Our RBAC model has roles and attributes - Admin, Developer, Operator, ReadOnly and you can map to your IdP groups via SAML/SCIM. We also support just-in-time provisioning. We can show the role mapping in the spreadsheet.
02:05 Laura Kim: SCIM is a must - we need group sync and de-provisioning. Any audit trails for SSO events?
02:12 Ravi Patel: Yes, SSO events are recorded in audit logs with actor, action, timestamp and affected resource. Logs include SAML assertions (redacted) and auth successes/failures. There are some small transcription quirks: sample was transcribed as 'sample' in earlier docs, but we will provide the raw fields.
02:30 Priya Sharma: Regarding audit log retention - we want 7 years for certain events and at least 1 year for others. What are your retention policies?
02:38 Maya Chen: Default retention in Hosted is 90 days for high-granularity operational logs, 7 years is a long tail and is usually handled by pushing logs out to customer's archival S3/Kinesis bucket. We can support TTL-based exports; the Trust Center will document recommended architecture for long-term retention.
03:00 Daniel Ortiz: Would you be able to stream to our on-prem SIEM? We have a secure tunnel and it's a hard requirement for production.
03:08 Ravi Patel: Yes, customers stream to on-prem via VPN or Direct Connect; we also support an agent that ships logs into your Kinesis or Kafka endpoint. For on-prem we typically validate firewall egress rules and sign certs.
03:25 Laura Kim: Controls mapping - we need to map your controls to our internal controls and to the SOC2/ISO control ids. Does Redwood provide a mapping template?
03:33 Maya Chen: We do, Ravi will populate a spreadsheet that maps Redwood control (e.g., access control, encryption-at-rest) to SOC 2 CC6, ISO A.9, etc. It will include evidence locations and expected artifacts.
03:45 Priya Sharma: A question on encryption in transit - TLS best practices? and mTLS?
03:50 Ravi Patel: All customer traffic is TLS 1.2+; internal service-to-service is mTLS in Dedicated and Private. For Hosted we can enable mTLS for customer-managed endpoints. We'll include cipher lists and cert rotation cadence in the package.
04:10 Ethan Cho: For CMK, are you able to use our KMS key with a customer-managed policy? we need to ensure Redwood can't decrypt without an IAM permission switch.
04:20 Maya Chen: For CMK we use envelope encryption; customer retains key control in their KMS. Redwood's service has IAM roles that can be conditionally granted decrypt on a per-environment basis. There is a small ops workflow for emergency access that is logged and requires approval. We'll document the emergency access escalation path.
04:40 Laura Kim: About trust center access - how long will the read-only account last and what artifacts are available?
04:48 Maya Chen: Typically 30 days by default but we can extend; artifacts include the SOC 2 report (redacted where necessary), ISO 27001 cert, penetration testing exec summaries, and a controls matrix. Some raw evidence (e.g., internal tickets) is available under NDA only.
05:05 Priya Sharma: Any third-party sub processors? We need a list and whether they are in-scope for SOC 2.
05:12 Maya Chen: Yes we publish subprocessors in the Trust Center; primary ones are AWS, Cloud vendor X for observability, and a CDN provider. We'll include the subprocessors list and their compliance posture.
05:28 Daniel Ortiz: Network-level question: can you pin upstream egress to our region to satisfy data residency?
05:34 Ravi Patel: We have region routing policies; requests can be pinned to eu-west-1 or us-east-1. For strict residency we recommend Dedicated or Private deployment. Hosted has region guarantees but customers with strict residency often go Dedicated.
05:50 Laura Kim: What about pen test windows and remediation verification?
05:55 Maya Chen: We publish an executive summary of our most recent pentest; for remediation verification we can share timelines and evidence, and for customers with Dedicated we can run joint tests under a scoping agreement.
06:10 Priya Sharma: Any questions about liability or contract language? we have clauses requiring data breach notification within 72 hours.
06:17 Maya Chen: Redwood's standard enterprise terms have a 72 hour notification SLA; we'll escalate to legal if you want additional contract language.
06:25 Ethan Cho: Are there known limitations to audit log fields (like request body is never in logs)?
06:30 Ravi Patel: We do not log request bodies that contain PII by default. Logs include metadata, request path, model id, latency, token counts, and a redacted user id. If you need additional fields we can discuss a limited-scope telemetry agreement.
06:45 Laura Kim: Ok good. Can you confirm the timeline to get the docs? we need to onboard before Jan 15 for pilot.
06:52 Maya Chen: We'll get the SOC2/ISO artifacts and Trust Center link by 12/10; controls mapping by 12/12; schedule the infra deep-dive the week of 12/15. Does that work?
07:05 Daniel Ortiz: Yes that aligns. Please also include any network egress rules and sample terraform for the KMS setup.
07:12 Ravi Patel: We'll include a sample terraform snippet for KMS and the CIDR ranges.
07:20 Laura Kim: Any final questions?
07:23 Maya Chen: Not from us. Thank you everyone. Recap: we'll send the trust center link and reports, Ravi will prepare the mapping and terraform snippets, then we schedule architecture deep-dive.
07:35 Priya Sharma: Thanks, talk soon.
07:38 [meeting ends]
notes: Customer requires SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 certs; NDA to access full artifacts
Redwood offers CMK via AWS KMS; Dedicated/Private options for stricter residency
Audit logs can be streamed to customer SIEM (Kinesis, S3, syslog)
Controls mapping spreadsheet will map Redwood controls to SOC/ISO control IDs
